metadata.title: Phase II of the LAMOST-Kepler/K2 Survey. II. Time Domain of Medium-resolution Spectroscopic Observations from 2018 to 2023

evidence.quote: This star, known as KIC 7881304, has been classified as a long-period variable by Yu et al. (2020).
Based on this, we consider KIC 7881304 a possible unbound high-velocity candidate.
Using the Galactic escape velocity curve, we identified one high-velocity star candidate that is not gravitationally bound to the Milky Way and 29 high-velocity star candidates that are bound.

values.condition: V_gc tabulated in Table 5 for uid G17065374200707 / EPIC 220496220; the star is labeled unbound. The Table 5 note calls column 7 the Galactic standard-of-rest velocity, while the text defines V_G as the total velocity from U, V, W.

notes: KIC 7881304: The prose explicitly calls this star a possible unbound high-velocity candidate (T:p11-b6) and the summary retains one unbound high-velocity candidate (T:p14-b4). The sole "unbound" row visible in Table 5 is uid G17065374200707 / KIC/EPIC 220496220 (I:p17-b4), but the paper does not explicitly cross-identify that row with KIC 7881304, and the table lists Times=8 whereas the text describes seven RV spectra. I group them as the paper's single unbound candidate while flagging the identifier inconsistency. The 29 high-velocity stars explicitly labeled bound are excluded.

KIC 7881304: The target appears as KIC 7881304 in the text (T:p11-b6), where it is described as the single unbound high-velocity candidate, and as uid G17065374200707 / EPIC 220496220 in the unbound row of Table 5 (T:p17-b4, I:p17-b4); I treated these as the same star because the supplied identifiers link them and the unbound label matches. The text reports seven spectra with an RV range of 181.8–349.2 km/s, whereas Table 5 gives Times=8 and RV=215.77 km/s. The tabulated V_gc=374.40 km/s also does not match the ~580 km/s weighted V_GC value indicated in Figure 8 (I:p12-b0), and Table 5's note describes column 7 as the Galactic standard-of-rest velocity. I therefore report the tabulated point values and the text's RV interval separately rather than reconciling them. No numerical bound/unbound probability is reported.
